places.name: LEGO

places.name: Lužická
places.description: Lužická is a residential street in the Vinohrady district of Prague lined with approximately 80 mature hackberry trees that form a natural canopy. The post recommends visiting during autumn when the leaves turn gold and amber to create a scenic tunnel of colors.

places.name: Corner Stories
places.description: Corner Stories is a vibrant café in Vršovice that mixes art-nouveau charm with farm-to-table fare and cozy vibes from morning coffee to evening drinks.

places.name: May Cafe
places.description: May Cafe is a colorful spot in Vinohrady serving hand-brews, brunch items, and signature drinks.

places.name: Linka
places.description: Linka is a bistro in Vinohrady serving sweet and savory crêpes, breakfast favorites, and good coffee in a distinctive, artsy interior.

places.name: Vnitroblock
places.description: Vnitroblock is a shared creative space in Holešovice where you can sip coffee, shop, and soak up edgy vibes.

places.name: Bullerbyn
places.description: Bullerbyn is a neighborhood spot in Vinohrady for breakfast, original dishes, coffee, and creative cocktails.

places.name: Ba-lăm
places.description: Ba-lăm offers specialty coffee and brunch all day with an emphasis on matcha, plant-based options, and a relaxed, family-friendly atmosphere.

places.name: Cocovanka
places.description: Cocovanka is described as a bohemian café in Malá Strana with wonderful decor and lovely lemonades and cafés.

places.name: Anežka
places.description: Anežka is a café-bar nestled within the Gothic St. Agnes Convent in Old Town that blends medieval architecture with modern style.

places.name: Cafefin
places.description: Cafefin is a lovely brunch spot right next to JZP where their savory croissant is recommended as to die for.

places.name: Ca Phe
places.description: Ca Phe is a café-bistro in Holešovice where Vietnamese cuisine meets European-style coffee.

places.name: Kampa
places.description: Kampa is a park recommended for its cute streets, riverside views, and a different side of Prague.

places.name: Botanical Garden
places.description: The Botanical Garden is a park where visitors can see giant pumpkin displays running until November 1.

places.name: U Stolu
places.description: U Stolu is a little café in Malá Strana recommended for its amazing drinks and food.

places.name: Magical Cavern
places.description: The Magical Cavern is a strange, colourful cave in Petřín that feels made for a spooky autumn day.

places.name: Kellyxir
places.description: Kellyxir is an alchemy-themed bar recommended for looking straight out of a witch's hideout.

places.name: Convent of St Agnes
places.description: The Convent of St Agnes is a historic convent recommended to escape chilly weather and explore medieval art inside.

places.name: Stromovka
places.description: Stromovka is a park recommended for relaxing when the trees turn golden and the park is covered in autumn leaves.

places.name: U Krále Brabantského
places.description: U Krále Brabantského is one of Prague's oldest taverns, dating back to 1375, recommended for dinner.

places.name: Dno Pytle
places.description: Dno Pytle is a pub located in central Prague owned by Dušan Makovský. The post recommends it because the owner has publicly and unapologetically expressed support for Israel.

places.name: @kuskolace
places.description: @kuskolace is a place in Prague recommended for koláč, described as soft, freshly baked dough with a sweet filling and crumble on top. The post advises visitors to expect a queue but states it is worth the wait.

places.name: Krafin
places.description: Krafin is a plant-based bakery that serves specialty coffee and its signature croissant-muffin hybrid. The post recommends it for trying seasonal pastries.

places.name: Umělecká zahrada
places.description: Umělecká zahrada is a sculpture-filled garden in Nusle featuring artistic details and a tucked-away feel. It is recommended as a place to explore during the fall.

places.name: Střelecký ostrov
places.description: Střelecký ostrov is a leafy island in the Vltava with riverside paths, colourful trees, and lovely views of Prague. The post suggests taking a walk there.

places.name: Kavárna U Raka
places.description: Kavárna U Raka is a tiny café located in the historic Nový Svět area within a charming old timber building. It is recommended for its homemade sweets.

places.name: Artyčok
places.description: Artyčok is a beautifully curated concept store featuring unique gifts and pieces from independent designers. The post recommends browsing this shop.

places.name: Lužická Street
places.description: Lužická Street is a pretty residential street in Vinohrady known for its beautiful golden trees. The post suggests walking down it to enjoy the fall foliage.

places.name: Joy Bakery
places.description: Joy Bakery offers pumpkin pastries as part of its seasonal Halloween special called The Pumpkin. It is recommended as a perfect stop for an autumn treat.

places.name: Lost Garden (Zahrada Ztracenka)
places.description: The Lost Garden (Zahrada Ztracenka) is a terraced garden located on the hillside near Albertov. The post recommends finding this location.

places.name: Grand Cru
places.description: Grand Cru is an elegant fine-dining restaurant serving modern European cuisine with an impressive wine selection. The post recommends booking dinner there.

places.name: AnonymouS Bar
places.description: AnonymouS Bar is a mysterious, theatrical cocktail bar in Old Town where drinks come with creative presentations. The post recommends having cocktails here.

places.name: Máj House of Fun

places.description: The National Museum (Národní muzeum) is one of Prague's most iconic landmarks and impressive Neo-Renaissance buildings located at the top of Wenceslas Square. The post recommends it for its spectacular façade, the Pantheon hall with bronze statues celebrating Czech history, and exhibitions covering archaeology and natural history.

places.name: Náměstí Míru
places.description: Náměstí Míru is a Christmas market in Vinohrady featuring around 60 stalls and a park for children to run in, recommended by the post as the primary choice for families due to lower prices and a local atmosphere.

places.name: Jiřího z Poděbrad
places.description: Jiřího z Poděbrad is a market where the playground transforms into a straw play area during Advent and features Ježíšek's chapel office for children to post Christmas wishes, making it the top choice for toddlers.

places.name: Old Town Square
places.description: Old Town Square hosts the city's largest Christmas market with an animal pen, a tree light show running hourly, and a viewing platform, recommended for families to visit on weekday mornings to avoid crowds.

places.name: Wenceslas Square
places.description: Wenceslas Square hosts one of Prague's two biggest Christmas markets and features Výtopna railway restaurant where model trains deliver drinks to tables, recommended for a unique dining experience.

places.name: Kampa
places.description: Kampa is a compact market under Charles Bridge featuring wooden puppets and glass figures, with the adjacent Kampa Park offering space for children to run.

places.name: Vinohradský Parlament
places.description: Vinohradský Parlament is a Czech restaurant located near Náměstí Míru that features a large indoor play corner with craft programs, recommended as a warm-up stop where parents can monitor children via an app.

places.name: Výtopna
places.description: Výtopna is a railway restaurant on Wenceslas Square where model trains run on 900 meters of track to deliver drinks to tables, recommended for its unique train feature rather than just the food.

places.name: Petřín funicular
places.address: Újezd up to the top of Petřín Hill
places.extracted_address: Újezd up to the top of Petřín Hill
places.description: The Petřín funicular is Prague's oldest funicular with new glass-sided cars that offers views over snowy rooftops and free rides for children under 15, recommended as a short, warm ride for city views.

places.name: Ovocný trh
places.description: Ovocný trh features a small outdoor ice skating rink that usually opens from early December until the end of January with free entry, recommended as an activity for children.

places.name: Prague Zoo
places.description: Prague Zoo stays open on Christmas Eve morning and charges children under 15 only one koruna that day, recommended for families to visit and hand gifts like carrots or apples to the animals.

places.name: Kampa Park
places.description: Kampa Park is located next to the Kampa market and provides space for children to run, recommended as a place to burn off energy after browsing the nearby stalls.

places.name: Křížovnické náměstí
places.description: Křížovnické náměstí is a street where a lamplighter in a 19th-century uniform lights gas lamps by hand every evening from Advent until December 23, recommended for children to walk alongside and chat with the lamplighter.

places.name: Bethlehem Chapel
places.description: Bethlehem Chapel houses a traditional Christmas exhibition with over 200 nativity scenes and a water-powered hammer where kids can crack walnuts, recommended as a warm-up stop that accepts cash only.

places.name: Charles Bridge
places.description: Charles Bridge is a historic bridge under which the Kampa market is located and where a lamplighter performs daily during Advent. The post recommends visiting to see the lamplighter light the gas lamps in uniform or to cross to Malá Strana.

places.name: Astronomical Clock
places.description: The Astronomical Clock is an attraction visible from a viewing platform in Old Town Square that features hourly shows of the apostles. The post recommends visiting at 11:00 on the hour as part of a family itinerary.

places.name: Chocolaterie BON BON
places.description: Chocolaterie BON BON is described as a chocolate lover's paradise offering dark, milk, white or caramel hot chocolate alongside handmade pralines and other chocolate specialities. The post recommends it as one of two spots in Prague for rich, thick hot chocolate.

places.name: Choco Café
places.description: Choco Café is a family-run chocolate café featuring over 70 types of handmade chocolate and serving rich, thick hot chocolate made with real chocolate. The post recommends it as one of two spots in Prague for rich, thick hot chocolate.

days.title: Arrival - three easy Old Town stops
days.hotel_notes: All three suggestions are optional around your actual arrival time. Feed, change and rest at the hotel first. KIDS means a child-friendly short visit, not necessarily a playroom; the baby mainly watches at sights. About 0.6 km between stops (8 minutes nominal walking; allow 15-20 with the stroller and crowds). No cross-city trip today.
noon: Arrival/check-in as travel allows; keep the usual nap and give the baby supervised floor time before going out.
afternoon: 1. KIDS - Old Town Hall and Astronomical Clock: 5-10 minutes outside to look at the clock. Skip the tower and do not wait in a dense crowd for the hourly display.
2. KIDS - Old Town Square Christmas market: a short look at the tree, lights and stalls, about 20-30 minutes. Leave if crowded; this is a family stroll, not active play.
3. KIDS - LEGO on Na Prikope: a warm 20-minute look at the large Prague models. Free shop visit, not a workshop or baby playroom; keep small pieces away from both under-threes.
evening: Early dinner and bedtime; do not extend the outing just to finish all three stops.

days.title: Trains, Green Butik and Kampa floor time
days.hotel_notes: One direction along the west bank: Andel -> Smichov -> Kampa. This is the longest cluster: about 1.8 km between stops (25 minutes nominal walking; allow 35-45 with the children). Green Butik is a quick adult stop, not counted as children's play. Confirm KC Kampa's volunteer-run opening the day before.
morning: 1. KIDS - Kingdom of Railways: start around 09:00 and allow 75-90 minutes for moving trains and the younger-child play areas. Better for the toddler; supervise the baby's separate needs.
2. Green Butik - Smichov: a 15-20-minute browse after the trains. It has seating and small children's toys, but parents should take turns rather than expect childcare.
noon: 3. KIDS - KC Kampa baby and toddler playroom: around 11:30, allow 45-60 minutes of parent-accompanied play and baby floor time. Bring lunch/food to warm in its kitchenette.
afternoon: Return to Hotel Leon D'Oro for the usual post-lunch nap, feeding and quiet time. No second district or shopping trip planned.

days.title: Letna tractors, transport and ONEDAY
days.hotel_notes: About 0.6 km between stops (8 minutes nominal walking; allow 15-20). These are two short child-friendly vehicle visits, not two full museum tours: Agriculture is the main outing and Technical is optional if energy is low. Both are on the same street. ONEDAY opens at noon on weekdays. Use transport up to Letna rather than pushing up the park stairs.
morning: 1. KIDS - National Museum of Agriculture: around 09:30, spend 60-75 minutes with the tractors, toddler push bikes and pedal tractors. This is not an infant soft-play room.

2. KIDS - National Technical Museum: next door, choose just 30-40 minutes in the transport hall for cars, planes and trains. Use the pram ramp to the right of the entrance; skip the mine and advanced activities.
noon: Lunch/snack and feeding break; keep the timing flexible rather than fill the gap with another attraction.
3. ONEDAY - Letna: from 12:00, a 15-20-minute browse of the small Czech women's clothing label. Take turns if the children need a break.
afternoon: Return to the hotel for the usual nap and baby floor time. Skip the optional museum or boutique if it would delay the nap; no separate Josefov outing.

days.title: Charles Bridge, a warm cafe and Kampa play
days.hotel_notes: About 1.1 km between stops (15 minutes nominal walking; allow 25-30 on cobbles). KC Kampa repeats intentionally: it is genuine baby/toddler play, not another adult sight. Check its volunteer-run opening before setting out. Cocovanka is a normal cafe break, not a verified play cafe.
morning: 1. KIDS - Charles Bridge: around 09:30, a short stroller stroll towards Mala Strana to watch boats and look at the statues. Keep the toddler close; skip a long crossing if icy, windy or crowded.
2. Cocovanka: aim for 10:15 or later for a warm drink and snack. Check current cafe opening; do not assume there are toys or supervised play.
noon: 3. KIDS - KC Kampa baby and toddler playroom: around 11:00, allow 60 minutes for both children to play with a parent. Its kitchenette can warm the children's food before returning.
afternoon: Return to Hotel Leon D'Oro for the usual post-lunch rest. Do not add a castle climb or a second shopping area.

days.title: Central LEGO models, NILA and train-served lunch
days.hotel_notes: About 1.2 km between stops (16 minutes nominal walking; allow 25-30). Museum of Bricks explicitly is NOT step-free: bring a carrier and confirm stroller arrangements. If that is impractical, replace stop 1 with the already-saved LEGO flagship rather than carry an occupied stroller downstairs. Ask Vytopna about first-floor stroller access and highchairs when reserving.
morning: 1. KIDS - Museum of Bricks Prague: from 10:00, a 45-60-minute look at the LEGO models. Mainly for the toddler to look at; supervise small parts and do not assume an under-three-safe building area.
2. NILA Lazarska: around 11:15, a short 15-20-minute boutique browse, not a children's activity.
noon: 3. KIDS - Vytopna Railway Restaurant: aim for an early lunch around 11:45-12:00. The table-serving model trains provide the toddler's second child-friendly stop; the baby can watch. Reserve/check access yourselves; this is a restaurant, not floor play.
afternoon: Return to the hotel for nap, feeding and supervised baby floor time. No extra mall or optician visit in the three-stop plan.

days.title: Aquarium, Panda Play and Tvorba in Holesovice
days.hotel_notes: About 1.0 km between stops (13 minutes nominal walking; allow 20-25). This combines the former separate Panda and aquarium days and avoids a cross-city shopping add-on. Panda's site was unreachable on November 27; its recent official indexed listing says ages 0-7 and daily 09:00-20:00. Reconfirm before going. Tvorba's published weekday opening starts at 12:00.
morning: 1. KIDS - Morsky svet aquarium: around 09:30, allow 45-60 minutes for fish and sharks. Both children can watch; stay with the accessible lower tanks if using the stroller and use a carrier for upstairs stairs.

2. KIDS - Panda Play, OC Stromovka: around 10:45, allow 60-75 minutes of active baby/toddler play, with a cafe/bistro break if useful. Stay with both children: drop-off is for over-threes, not your toddler.
noon: 3. Tvorba Store: from 12:00, a 15-20-minute look at the Czech women's clothing labels. Check current opening and exact stock; this is the adult stop, not a third children's attraction.
afternoon: Return to the hotel for the normal nap and quiet time. Do not add a long Stromovka park circuit in December.

days.title: Vinohrady boutique, family play-lunch and Christmas market
days.hotel_notes: Final night. Walk west along Korunni rather than backtracking: about 1.3 km between stops (17 minutes nominal walking; allow 25-30). Reserve family lunch and ask about playroom space. The restaurant's rules allow under-threes only WITH a parent; neither child can be left with the hostess. The market is a short family stroll, not a second playroom.
morning: 1. NILA Vinohrady, Korunni 91: around 10:30, a short boutique visit. The brand also lists an outlet at the same address with Saturday 10:00-16:00 opening; ask what is available rather than assume a discount.
noon: 2. KIDS - Vinohradsky Parlament: family lunch around 11:30 when the weekend play programme starts. One parent accompanies the children in the playroom; take turns eating rather than rely on unattended care.
3. KIDS - Namesti Miru Christmas market: after lunch, 15-20 minutes for the lights, stalls and wooden-toy browsing, then leave before the children's nap is pushed back.
afternoon: Return to Hotel Leon D'Oro for nap and quiet play. Pack after resting instead of adding another outing.

days.title: Departure - three optional central stops
days.hotel_notes: Departure day; no overnight stay. These are options only if check-out and flight times leave a comfortable window, not a commitment before an unknown flight. About 1.0 km between stops (13 minutes nominal walking; allow 20-25). The LEGO repeat is intentional and easy to shorten. Garden winter opening is 08:00-19:00, but usable play depends on weather.
morning: 1. KIDS - LEGO on Na Prikope: an optional 15-20-minute repeat after its 10:00 opening. Skip all stops if travelling earlier.

2. KIDS - Franciscan Garden: a 15-20-minute toddler movement/playground break if dry and safe, with the baby warm in the stroller. If icy or wet, replace it with the already-saved Museum of Bricks only if the carrier/access arrangements work.
3. Bata - Wenceslas Square: a short final shoe browse if time permits; check Sunday opening and keep a firm departure cut-off.
noon: Check-out/luggage and departure according to your actual travel arrangements. No prepaid attraction or late reservation planned.
